newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan to pay $680 mln for private power by 1998.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to pay $680 mln for private power by 1998.

text.p: Pakistan will face an annual bill of $680 million for privately supplied power when projects producing about 3,220 megawatts of electricity come on stream in 1998, a government official said on Wednesday.

Shahid Hassan Khan, special economic assistant to Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto, told reporters the state-owned Water and Power Development Authority had signed power purchase agreements worth a total of $588 million a year so far.
The authority had agreeed to buy the electricity at an average rate of 6.5 cents per kilowatt hour.
The state-run Karachi Electric Supply Corporation had signed similar agreements worth $92 million a year, he added.

He said the government would also have to pay for additional fuel imports worth $144 million a year from 1998 to supply fuel oil to thermal plants under commitments outlined in an energy policy introduced in April 1994.
Khan said that of the total 3,220-MW of electricity generated by the new plants, about 1,225 MW would be from gas-fired plants not requiring imported fuel oil.

Pakistan has now stopped approving private power projects that depend on imported energy. "In the months to come we will still be issuing letters of support for projects based on indigenous fuel," Khan said.
Pakistan needs an estimated $50 billion of investment in the power sector to meet growing electricity demand over the next two decades, officials say.
They foresee most of the investment coming from private sector joint ventures in response to government incentives.
Pakistan, with an installed capacity of 12,530 MW, currently faces a gap of about 2,000 MW during peak periods.
